title: To amend the FISA Amendments Act of 2008 to extend the authorities of title VII of the Foreign Intelligence Surveillance Act of 1978 through April 30, 2026, and for other purposes.

claims.note: Source attributes the authorization to 'the Attorney General and the Director of National Intelligence' acting jointly, carried out by elements of the intelligence community; the NSA is never named in the statute. Operationally conventional but extrinsic to the source text.  [2026-09-02 wrap-up re-audit] Prose no longer names the NSA. The summary now attributes the authorization to the Attorney General and the Director of National Intelligence acting jointly, in the statute's own words.

resolution: RE-AUDITED 2026-09-02 (wrap-up). The whole "lets the NSA collect" family is gone: 50 U.S.C. 1881a names the NSA and the CIA ZERO times, and the authorization, the provider directives and the querying procedures all run to the Attorney General and the Director of National Intelligence. Root cause was scripts/prompts.js RULE 8, whose own "Good" exemplar told the model to write exactly this sentence and labelled it sourced to 1881a; fixed in e5cc7474 with a new failure pattern #10. Prose rewritten in-conversation from a fresh read of the enrolled text and the statute, then put through a hostile Sonnet source-only pass which returned 5 blocking and 4 advisory findings, ALL accepted and fixed in a second pass: the (j)(3)/(c)(2) precondition had been dropped, making a conditioned authorization read as a standing power; 1881a(b)(4) had been generalised into a claim about everything subsection (b) forbids, dropping (b)(2), (b)(5) and (b)(6); the FBI prior-approval rule was stated with no carve-out; the (i)(1)(A) directive was truncated before its secrecy and minimum-interference qualifier; "the Court reviews procedures rather than individual queries" was an inference by omission, replaced by (j)(2)(D) stated positively; and the Reforming Intelligence and Securing America Act string was attributed to paragraph (1), which the bill elides, when only paragraph (2) spells it out. Two long-standing OMISSIONs closed at the same time: Section 1(b)'s amendments to Section 404(b), and the paragraph (2) amendment to the 18 U.S.C. 2511 note. qa-source-verify clean, 0 open flags.
notes: Reference-dependent bill: the enacted text (PL 119-84) only moves the Title VII repeal date to April 30, 2026 and makes conforming cross-reference edits; all substantive 'what Section 702 does' claims were judged against the registered referencedSource 50 U.S.C. 1881a (2024 edition). No material errors. Recurring minor flag: the analysis names 'the NSA' as the collecting/compelling actor, but the statute attributes authorization and provider directives to the Attorney General and the Director of National Intelligence (collection carried out by unnamed elements of the intelligence community) — conventional but extrinsic to source. Stage/vote cross-check consistent: bill text 'Approved April 18, 2026' + 'Public Law 119-84' match stage=signed / likelihood=Enacted (note: bill-text legislative history dates House passage Apr. 16, whereas cache votes[] list Apr. 17 — structured-field discrepancy, not a prose claim).
